observation: One related living-provider mode-dependent container-exchange whole policy at most. Qualifying adult Cow/Goat can request fresh default milk without mutating a finite provider stock; creative existence-sensitive inventory admission differs from survival bucket debit and hand-or-overflow output. Consumer cure/container return is traced as output use and qualification, not an independently novel cure mechanism.

Cow whole94 and Goat interaction192-207 are read. Both literal BUCKET&&!isBaby paths play sound before constructing default milk, call same createFilledResult and set actual hand, then sidedSuccess. Cow breed/AI and Goat fallback food sound do not become extra resource policies; no own milk stock/feeding/cooldown debit is shown.

No own authoritative-server guard in those interaction branches. Enclosing dispatch, permissions, prediction and callbacks are not expanded; the source branch alone proves neither exploitable client duplication nor unlimited current-survival acquisition.

Items registers milk as MilkBucketItem with bucket crafting remainder and maxstack1. Default-instance invokes ItemStack(this)->count1 constructor, delegate lookup/forgeInit and damage hooks. This is a source construction chain; loaded registry/capability/current-player acquisition are separate.

createFilledResult default enables creative duplicate check. Creative returns the exact input reference unchanged; contains across items/armor/offhand can skip adding output entirely. Its predicate compares item/tag/caps without count; add return ignored. Sound and success can therefore coexist with no positive output request or inventory delta.

Noncreative createFilledResult shrinks input first. If empty, returns output to the subsequent hand assignment; otherwise inventory-add may mutate output, and false invokes Toss with remaining output. Output request, actual hand replacement, positive inventory delta, world admission and intended-player later pickup are separate evidence.

Inventory merge capacity checks stackability/maxstack/maxcontainer and item/tag/caps. addResource copies original stack preserving caps into empty destination, count0 then grow. Main/offhand/general slot selection and fallback free slot are ordered, not player preference or lossless arbitrary-backend guarantee.

Inventory.add ordinary loop returns whether the last attempted iteration reduced remainder. Earlier partial progress can end with false and a remaining stack; creative no-progress may clear count and returntrue without storing. Damaged-stack branch separately uses a free main slot or creative discard. No universal positive-admission receipt from boolean alone.

Living setItemInHand selects main/offhand or throws; Player setItemSlot verifies then mutates inventory before onEquipItem. A returned filled result is not itself committed slot state; failures/hooks/reentrancy/authoritative sync are outside this bounded path.

Overflow two-argument Player.drop invokes onPlayerTossEvent. Temporary captureDrops list is installed then reset null without visible restoration of an earlier capture collector in this method. Three-arg drop constructs ItemEntity/pickupDelay40 and does not spawn it itself. Toss cancel returnsnull; otherwise only nonclient requests unchecked addFreshEntity. No native loss/reentrancy exploit is asserted.

createFilledResult calls drop(output,false), so Toss includeNamefalse leaves this constructor path without thrower assignment. It does not set an intended-player ownership target or establish actual UUID pickup; motion, delay and nonnull event entity are not positive admitted-world custody.

Milk.use only requests startUsingItem/consume result. DRINK/duration32 do not close the enclosing use interruption/tick/finish lifecycle or prove elapsed real time. Full MilkBucketItem read is not full native use engine audit.

Milk finish server cure occurs before ServerPlayer criterion/stat and before survival-player shrink. This retains the curative stack type during matching. All source-order statements assume previous callbacks complete normally; neither criterion nor stat proves paid resource or effect removal.

curePotionEffects server-only iteration requires item-type curative match and noncanceled per-effect Remove, then onEffectRemoved, iterator.remove and dirty. No harmful-only filter appears; matching beneficial effects can also be removed. Removal helper requests attributes/passenger packets; actual listeners/network/effect-attribute internals are not all audited.

Milk ignores cure bool; survival-player shrink follows even for zero matching effects or all vetoed removals. Nonplayer and instabuild branches do not shrink through this conditional; empty result returns fresh BUCKET, otherwise original stack. No atomic cost-benefit/refund or universal one-bucket delivery claim.

Effect curative null lazily asks effect defaults; Forge default returns fresh milk list. Instance setters can replace it including empty. isCurativeItem uses isSameItem only, unlike creative inventory.contains tags/caps. These are different authorization equivalence relations, not per-stack UUID or per-source effect ownership.

Full curative interface writes each stack save; bounded read helper accepts CurativeItems TAG_LIST then reads compound entries and replaces list. Wrong list element type can produce an empty compound-list view; exact getter implementation not re-expanded, so no malformed-save or unknown-item recovery promise. Absent list allows lazy default conditional on other callers, not a full save roundtrip.
